questions.question: Explain the concept of overflow in binary addition.
questions.solution_html:
• Overflow in binary addition occurs when the sum of two binary numbers exceeds
  • the range that can be represented with the given number of bits.

questions.solution_html:
• Explain the concept of toggling in a JK flip-flop.
  • A JK flip-flop toggles when both inputs, J and K, are set to 1. This means that on the next
  • clock pulse, the output Q will flip to 1if it was 0, or to 0 if it was 1
  • . This behavior makes the JK flip-flop useful for applications like counters

questions.question: Explain how a decoder is used for memory address selection in computer systems. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how a decoder is used for memory address selection in computer
  • systems. - by converting a binary memory address from the CPU into a single
  • active output line that enables a particular memory chip or a specific word line
  • within a chip. It takes 𝑛 input lines representing the binary address and
  • activates one of its 2 𝑛 output lines, where only the selected line is active (e.g.,
  • high) at any given time. This ensures that data is read from or written to only
  • the correct memory cell.
  • [U] /
  • [CO3]

questions.question: Apply De Morgan’s theorems to each of the following expressions (i ) [(A + B + C) D]′ (ii) (ABC + DEF)′ (iii) (AB′+ C′D + EF)′.
questions.solution_html:
• Application of De Morgan’s theorem 2 marks each
  • (i) [(A+B+C)D]′=(A+B+C)′+D′= (A′⋅B′⋅C′)+D′= A′⋅B′⋅C′+D′
  • (ii) (ABC+DEF)′=(ABC)′⋅(DEF)′= (A′+B′+C′)⋅(D′+E′+F′)
  • (iii) [AB′+C′D+EF]′= (AB′)′⋅(C′D)′⋅(EF)′ =(A′+B)⋅(C+D′)⋅(E′+F′)
